questions.prompt: 100bb, 4-bet pot, flop 9s 4d 2c, you have KK and face a bet. Best default?

choices.text: Continue, usually by getting the rest in.
Fold. A nine is too scary
Call and fold the turn on a blank

questions.explanation: Dry nine-high does not beat kings in a 4-bet pot.

questions.prompt: Same pot, you have A5s and missed. They bet. Best default?

choices.text: Fold. Your bluff 4-bet candidate has little equity and little room.
Raise and call a jam with no pair

questions.explanation: The 4-bet bluff needed a fold earlier. On this flop it is a give-up.

questions.prompt: You are all-in preflop with QQ against a 100bb jam from the button. You should…

choices.text: Accept the runout. There is no more decision.

questions.explanation: The decision was the call. Play the board honestly when you review it. Do not invent new actions.

questions.prompt: A wet flop in a 4-bet pot with AK and no pair, facing an all-in…

choices.text: Depends on the price and the range. It is not an automatic call just because you 4-bet.
Is always a fold, even for a tiny price

questions.explanation: Low SPR pushes you in with equity, but a board that hits sets and straights can make ace-high a fold if the price is bad.
